company_items.summary: AutoZone reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — 145 basis points of gross margin tailwind from tariff refunds and 105 basis points from a non-cash LIFO benefit inflated the number. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% versus expectations of plus 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80 to $90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex directly in the high-growth robotics and Physical AI ecosystem.

MillerKnoll reported fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and importantly the beat holds up even excluding tariff refunds — stripping out the 11-cent tailwind leaves EPS at 42 cents, still well above consensus. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88 to $4.03 billion from $3.93 to $4.13 billion, while EPS guidance was left unchanged.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a leadership transition with no financial results attached.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% against an expected 13.85%. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressures squeezing household budgets as headwinds, and expects a relatively flat retail sales environment in fiscal 2027 without formal guidance until later this fall. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory, structural cost actions underway, and a roughly 75% surge in North American towable RV order backlog year-over-year.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive Phase trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in participants. This is a significant clinical readout that validates VK2735 as a competitive obesity asset. The result is likely to generate broad interest across the GLP-1 and obesity drug space.

sectors: RV and discretionary consumer space faces headwinds per THOR Industries commentary — stubborn rates, fuel costs, and inflation are keeping retail soft. The GLP-1 and obesity drug sector gets a positive boost from VKTX's VK2735 weight loss data. Robotics and Physical AI see a strategic deal with CGNX acquiring RealSense.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is the Tuesday September 22nd pre-market earnings note covering six names reporting before the open. Let's run through what matters.

Starting with AutoZone — the headline EPS beat looks good at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but do not be fooled by the quality. The entire beat was manufactured by 145 basis points of gross margin help from tariff refunds and another 105 basis points from a non-cash LIFO benefit. Strip those out and the print is far less impressive. Domestic comps badly missed at plus 1.6% versus expectations of plus 3.1%, and operating expenses worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management tried to add color by noting sales improved in the back half of the quarter, but this is a low-quality beat and the market should treat it that way.

MillerKnoll is the opposite story — a beat that actually holds up under scrutiny. They came in at 53 cents versus 36 cents expected, and even after removing the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind you're still at 42 cents, six cents above consensus. Orders rose 3.5% year-over-year which is constructive. The knock is a sales miss and a trimmed full-year revenue guidance range, though EPS guidance was left untouched. Mixed but leaning better than feared.

THOR Industries is the clear miss of the morning. EPS came in at 78 cents versus 87 expected, gross margins collapsed 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, and management's commentary painted a tough consumer picture — stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, inflation squeezing budgets. They expect flat retail in fiscal 2027 and won't give formal guidance until later in the fall. The one silver lining is that North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year, suggesting demand could recover, but near-term this is a bearish print.

Cognex is making a bold move, acquiring RealSense — the leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly 500 million dollars upfront. RealSense is growing revenues over 50% year-over-year. This is a strategic bet on the robotics and Physical AI buildout and puts Cognex in a high-growth lane.

Pentair named a new CFO, Bob Hau, effective November 1st. He brings experience from Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Routine transition, no financial catalyst.

The standout mover this morning is Viking Therapeutics — shares are spiking pre-market on positive trial data for their GLP-1 obesity drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss. That is a clinically meaningful result and will put Viking firmly on the map as a serious competitor in the obesity space. Watch for sympathy moves across the GLP-1 universe.

Bottom line for today: it is a stock-picker's tape. No macro catalyst is dominating. VKTX is the headline momentum trade. AZO's beat may fade on quality concerns. THO looks challenged near-term. Stay selective.
